publisher: Human Reproduction (Oxford University Press); National Institute of Environmental Health Sciences study
vintage: North Carolina Early Pregnancy Study, 1982-1986 births
title: Length of human pregnancy and contributors to its natural variation
authors: Jukic, Baird, Weinberg, McConnaughey and Wilcox (2013), Human Reproduction 28(10)
universe: 125 singleton live births with the day of ovulation measured from daily urine hormones
geography: United States (one state's cohort; the figure is biological, not a place rate)
limits: Measured from ovulation, which the game's conception date stands for; obstetric gestation counted from the last menstrual period runs about two weeks longer (285 days at the median in the same table). One cohort of 125 births.

fromOvulation.quote: The median time from ovulation to birth was 268 days (38 weeks, 2 days).
fromOvulation.rangeQuote: The ovulation-based gestational ages for the 125 singleton live births ranged from 208 to 284 days
fromOvulation.tableRow: Table I, all births, ovulation: mean 267 (SD 10); percentiles 10th 253, 25th 262, 50th 268, 75th 275, 90th 280

use: renewalGestationDays: the median, 268 days; the spread is the 25th to 75th percentile, 262 to 275 days.
